title: Make a tiny book from one sheet of paper
description: One sheet of paper, folded and snipped just once, becomes a real little book with eight pages — small enough to fit in your pocket and big enough for a whole story.

body.heading: Fold, fold, snip
paragraphs: Fold your sheet in half, then in half again, then in half again, pressing every fold flat with your thumbnail. Open it up: you should see eight boxes, like a chocolate bar.
A grown-up makes one careful snip along the middle fold. Then fold the sheet into a star, push the ends together, and wrap the pages round — suddenly it is a book!

body.heading: Fill your tiny book
paragraphs: Page one is your cover: a title and a picture. Then one sentence and one drawing per page tells a whole story in seven tiny steps.
Make a pocket library: a weather book, a joke book, a book of your cat's adventures. Tiny books love company.

takeaway: Fold one sheet, snip once, and you have an eight-page pocket book — one sentence and one drawing per page tells the whole story.
ageGuidance: Ages 6-12; younger children (6-8) need a grown-up for the snip and the tricky fold.
materials: One sheet of A4 or letter paper
supervision: A grown-up must do or closely supervise the single scissor cut and help with the final fold.
safetyNotes: Scissors are for the grown-up or used sitting down with supervision — no walking with scissors.
Press folds with a thumbnail, not against skin or eyes.
Keep finished tiny books away from babies, who may chew paper.
screenFreeExtension: Tell the tiny book's story out loud as a play: one page, one scene, with voices for every character.
